20.$description: Primary press in light: action-primary 85% toward the page, in oklch.

75.$description: Primary press in dark: action-primary 85% toward the page, in oklch.

neutral.$description: Achromatic neutrals, named by HSL lightness percent. Only the values the themes use exist.

white.$description: White at fixed opacities, for washes and hairlines over any dark surface.

8.$description: The most white a dark rim carries: the top edge of a panel (border-rim-top), and the kbd chip.

38.$description: Input boundary: 3.4:1 or better on every dark surface.

black.$description: Black at fixed opacities, for washes, hairlines and shadows over any light surface.

45.$description: Input boundary: 3.3:1 or better on every light surface.

status.$description: Inside the sRGB gamut, so every display shows the same colour.

2-5.$description: Tailwind's 2.5: horizontal padding of small buttons and text inputs.

3-5.$description: Tailwind's 3.5: horizontal padding of large buttons.

2xs.$description: The corner of a coverage strip's cell: a quarter of the 4px edge's roundness on a sliver of about 6px (DECISIONS 153, consent row 6).

control.$description: Control heights. md is the app default; data-density="compact" shifts one step down.

2xl.$description: A control at the touch size on every pointer: Castle's icon button, select and filter triggers and option chips (DECISIONS 154). The first rung above xl; compact steps it down to xl.

3xl.$description: Castle's button, and the narrow switch row and tab (DECISIONS 154). Compact steps it down to 2xl.

4xl.$description: The switch row from 720px wide, and the step compact takes a 56 control down to (DECISIONS 154: the approved prototype's own 52, which a 36px tile in 6px of padding and two 1px edges cannot make at 48). Compact steps it down to 3xl.

5xl.$description: The large button, and the tab bar of an app's own navigation (DECISIONS 154). Compact steps it down to 4xl.

6xl.$description: The least height of a button whose label is two lines (DECISIONS 154). Compact steps it down to 5xl.

menu-row.$description: The plate of a Menu, Select or Combobox row (the command menu's is size-control-xl, 40). The row is 4px taller: each row carries 2px above and below its plate, so the 4px gap between plates is drawn inside the rows and neighbouring hit areas touch. Compact steps it down to 32.

menu-row-touch.$description: The least height of a row's hit area on a coarse pointer.

indicator.$description: The underline of the active tab in a horizontal tab bar. There is no vertical bar anywhere: the active row, a selected table row and vertical tabs take a plate, a wash or a pill instead.

description-label.$description: The label column of a DescriptionList: fixed, never sized to its longest label, so every list on a page shares one value edge and a long label wraps inside it.

field-label-inline.$description: The label column of an inline-label form row (InlineField): a short word in 14px mono ("subject", "message") fits it, and every row of one form shares one field edge. DECISIONS 162 V10 and R12.

track.$description: The track of Progress and Slider.

dot.$description: Status dots and the radio's checked dot.

choice-mark.$description: The check glyph inside a checkbox.

kbd.$description: Keyboard-key height, everywhere a Kbd appears.

table-row.$description: Default table row height; compact and touch densities override it.

code-line-height.$description: Line height of code blocks, independent of body text.

underline-offset.$description: Link underline offset: fixed, so it sits the same under every link.

slider-length.$description: Default length of a vertical slider; apps can override it.

dialog-width.$description: Dialog width, capped by the viewport.

sheet-width.$description: Side sheet width, capped by the viewport.

command-width.$description: Command menu width, capped by the viewport.

dialog-width-wide.$description: A wide dialog's width, capped by the viewport: 992px (DECISIONS 158, Q1), 118 characters of Geist Mono at 14px rounded up, kept in px.

search-trigger.$description: The search button's width from 720, shaped like a field (DECISIONS 155, R5). Below 720 it is a square icon button.

search-logo-width.$description: The leading slot of a search result that shows a brand's logo: 96 by 48, so the row is 60 with 6px above and below (DECISIONS 155, R9).

search-logo-height.$description: Height of the logo slot in a search result row.

search-pack-width.$description: The leading slot of a search result that shows a product's picture: 48 by 60, so the row is 72 with 6px above and below (DECISIONS 155, R9).

search-pack-height.$description: Height of the picture slot in a search result row.

toast-width.$description: Toast width, capped by the viewport.

popup-max-height.$description: Maximum height of a scrolling popup list, such as the command list.

list-width.$description: The list column of a list with a preview pane, fixed: a two-line row fits beside a 16px glyph. The pane takes the rest, space-4 away; below this plus that gap plus size-breakpoint-container the pane is pushed instead.

header.$description: The sticky bar: its border box, with its hairline inside. The top safe area is padding above it, added by the layout CSS.

tab-bar.$description: The phone tab bar, its hairline inside, before the bottom safe area.

row.$description: The least height of a link row on the page, directory or big (DECISIONS 152, consent row 3): the link itself, with its 1px rule above it outside. Not the header's or the tab bar's role, though the value is the same. A big row in its two-column form takes space-16.

sidebar-width.$description: The app sidebar from the large breakpoint; also a page's own aside, so one side-column width serves both.

rail-width.$description: The rail, from the medium breakpoint to the large.

page-width.$description: The inner row, gutters inside: the header's row and a data page.

prose-width.$description: A prose page's text column, on the row's start edge and never centred: about 72 characters of Geist at 16/24.

gutter.$description: The row's inline padding. Apps use the derived --basalt-gutter, which steps to size-gutter-narrow under the medium breakpoint.

gutter-narrow.$description: The row's inline padding under the medium breakpoint.

section-gap.$description: The space between a page's sections from the large breakpoint (1024). Apps use the derived --basalt-section-gap, which steps to size-section-gap-md from 720 to 1023 and size-section-gap-narrow under 720.

section-gap-md.$description: The space between a page's sections from the medium breakpoint (720) to the large.

section-gap-narrow.$description: The space between a page's sections under the medium breakpoint.

display-measure.$description: The widest line of display type, in the headline's own em: about 28 characters of Geist at 600, so a headline is a block and never a strip across the row. In Swift it is the number of ems (13), for a frame's maximum width.

breakpoint-md.$description: Below it: the phone (the tab bar, the menu sheet, the narrow gutter). A media query cannot read a token, so CSS writes this number beside a lint exception that names the token.

breakpoint-lg.$description: From it, the sidebar; below it, down to the medium breakpoint, the rail.

breakpoint-container.$description: A component's own width, in a container query: a description list stacks and a chart goes narrow below it.

breakpoint-container-sm.$description: A component's own width, in a container query, below which a button's two lines stay two lines: from it up to size-breakpoint-container the label and its note share one line (DECISIONS 154, D11b). A container query cannot read a token, so CSS writes this number beside a lint exception that names the token.

breakpoint-container-lg.$description: A component's own width, in a container query, below which panels stop sharing one seat and a bar of tabs drops from 56 to 48 (DECISIONS 154, X6 and D12). A container query cannot read a token, so CSS writes this number beside a lint exception that names the token.

chart-line.$description: An observed line and the plan stroke in a chart.

chart-mark.$description: A chart marker's diameter, or its side; the diamond has the same area.

cut.$description: The surface-coloured cut between a mark in front and what it crosses: a chart's marker ring and the plan's cut out of a bar, and the meter's tick.

hatch-pitch.$description: The pitch of the hatch that marks missing data: 1px lines at 45 degrees, this far apart.

chart-bar-max.$description: The widest a chart bar is; a bar is 60% of its day.

chart-bar-min.$description: The narrowest a chart bar is.

chart-dash.$description: The dash of a chart's second series (6 on, size-chart-dash-gap off), and the pitch of the third series' round dots.

chart-dash-gap.$description: The gap in a chart's dashed second series.

chart-plot.$description: A chart plot's height at every width.

chart-plot-sm.$description: The second, shorter plot height: the phase chart's trend. A plot is 240px, or this (DECISIONS 153, vote 11 and consent row 5).

chart-row.$description: A marks row's height, a default the app can set: one kind of reading across a run of days (DECISIONS 153, consent row 10).

diagram-node.$description: The least width of a node's track in a diagram's drawn layout; a track is also as wide as its widest unbreakable word, measured (DECISIONS 281).

diagram-table.$description: The least width of a schema diagram's table; a table is also as wide as its widest row on one line, measured (DECISIONS 281).

diagram-lane.$description: A data flow diagram's lane-name column, at the start of the drawn layout (DECISIONS 281).

diagram-step.$description: A sequence diagram's message row: the line at its middle, the number and label above it, the note below (DECISIONS 281).

diagram-head.$description: A diagram's arrowhead, its length and its width, for every kind of line (DECISIONS 281).

diagram-activation.$description: The width of an activation bar on a sequence diagram's lifeline (DECISIONS 306, 1.0).

diagram-foot.$description: The room a cardinality mark takes at a foreign key line's end; no elbow starts inside it (DECISIONS 306, 1.0).

diagram-guide-dash.$description: A sequence diagram's lifeline dash, on and off (4 on 4 off), unlike a message's 6 on 4 off (DECISIONS 281).

diagram-bead.$description: A diagram pulse's bead, along the line (DECISIONS 292); never more than two fifths of the line's visible length.

diagram-flow.$description: From one flow cut to the next on a diagram's live line (DECISIONS 292): a cut is size-cut, so 10 on, 2 off.

meter-marker.$description: A range meter's marker: a dot, ringed size-cut in the colour of the surface (DECISIONS 153, consent row 14).

stage-headroom.$description: The top of a stage the art keeps quiet for the bar: size-header (56) plus space-6 (24). The top safe area is added by the layout CSS. No pixel of it passes art-quiet-limit, and a stage declares that the product's headroom check passed.

amount.$description: The ink of a button's amount ("Add to cart $49"), a step quieter than its label (DECISIONS 154, D11b). Used only on the variants whose ink holds 4.5:1 at this opacity on every surface the button can sit on (primary, secondary, outline); ghost and danger keep full ink.

photo.$description: 3:2. Photographs and drawn scenes in the flow. The default.

6xl.$description: Display type from 1024, and the hero from 720 to 1023: the fixed step the display role is made of (docs/foundations.md, Display type).

7xl.$description: The hero from 1024: the fixed step the hero role is made of. A page writes the role, never this step, on a phone.

hero-narrow.$description: The hero under 720 (a role's phone value, not a step of the scale): sized so most words fit the 288px row at 44px; a word that does not fit breaks.

display-narrow.$description: The display role under 720 (a role's phone value, not a step of the scale).

blur.$description: Backdrop blur. Use the chrome class once per viewport: translucent layers never stack.

chrome.$description: The blur behind a sticky header bar (basalt-chrome), with surface-chrome as its fill. No saturate and no brightness filter. The only blur in Basalt. Web only: native bars use the platform bar material or stay opaque.

duration.$description: Exits run at 0.75 of their entry. Loops (the group at the end) are not entries and are not on this scale. figure and stagger belong to a figure (an entrance, a travel), not to a control.

confirm.$description: How long a confirmation holds before it returns to rest: a copy button's "Copied" and an icon button's done check (DECISIONS 154, D11c). A hold, not an animation: it is the same with or without reduced motion.

figure.$description: A figure's own motion: each mark of a page's one entrance, and the longest leg of a travel the eye follows. Never a control, popup, panel, page or block. Under reduced motion 100ms.

stagger.$description: The step between the marks of one figure entering, shrunk so every start falls within duration-slow of the first. Under reduced motion 0.

diagram.$description: A diagram's own motion (DECISIONS 292), when its author asks for it (motion="animated"). They time nothing but a diagram, and they do not collapse under reduced motion: nothing they time runs there. rest is a hold, as confirm is.

line-min.$description: The shortest a traced line takes to draw (a line takes its length at speed-diagram-trace, never under this nor over line-max).

line-max.$description: The longest a traced line takes to draw.

stagger.$description: Between one traced line's start and the next. It shrinks by one factor when an entrance would pass duration-diagram-limit.

step.$description: Between one sequence message's start and the next. It shrinks to fit the limit, as the stagger does.

limit.$description: An entrance ends inside it (WCAG 2.2.2's five seconds): the stagger or the step shrinks to fit, and no line's own duration changes.

leg-min.$description: The shortest leg of a packet (a leg takes its length at speed-diagram-packet, never under this nor over leg-max).

leg-max.$description: The longest leg of a packet.

rest.$description: A mover's rest at a stop, while the stop holds its arrival step. A hold, not an animation.

pause.$description: Between two runs of a pulse; and before the loops resume after a trace ends.

repeat.$description: Between a repeating packet landing and its next start.

loop.$description: Loops: they repeat while work is happening, so they may run longer than an entry. Under reduced motion a spinner fades instead of moving, and a loop is never cut to the 100ms floor, or it flickers.

ring.$description: One turn of the ring spinner.

braille.$description: One full cycle of the braille spinner's ten frames, 80ms a frame, stepped, not interpolated.

fade.$description: The reduced-motion fade that replaces a moving spinner, and the breathing line of a loading Sparkline.

ambient.$description: The middle period of a page's one ambient loop (opacity only, in its art): each mark runs 0.6 to 1.4 times it, with its own phase. Not run under reduced motion, in forced colours or in print.

speed.$description: Speeds in pixels a second, plain numbers (as opacity and aspect are). A diagram's motion only (DECISIONS 292).

trace.$description: A traced line's drawing, clamped by duration-diagram-line-min and -line-max.

packet.$description: A packet's leg (4ms a pixel), clamped by duration-diagram-leg-min and -leg-max.

pulse.$description: A pulse's bead along its route.

flow.$description: A flow line's march: its cuts move toward the head.

ease.$description: No overshoot anywhere. out: entries and moves that answer input. in: exits, at 0.75 of the entry. in-out: rest-to-rest travel the eye follows, and loop pulses. linear: spinners.

linear.$description: Spinner loops only. Entries do not use it.
